ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two rays starting from the same point on the left, r1 is a horizontal ray to the right, and r2 is a ray slanting upward to the right. Three squares are placed side by side on the horizontal ray r1, with side lengths gradually increasing from left to right; the upper-left vertex of each square lies on the slanted ray r2. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method: take the common endpoint of the two rays as the origin, take r1 as the positive x-axis, and write r2 as the line y=mx. If the left side of a certain square is at x and its side length is s, then its upper-left vertex is (x,s), and it is on y=mx, so s=mx. The next adjacent square starts at x+s, so its side length is m(x+s)=mx+ms=s(1+m). Therefore the side lengths of adjacent squares form a geometric sequence with common ratio 1+m. It is known that the side lengths of the two smallest squares are 20 and 22, so 1+m=22/20=1.1. The side length of the largest square is 22×1.1=24.2.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/linear-slope recurrence. From the image, take the common endpoint of the rays as the origin, let ray r1 be the positive x-axis, and let ray r2 be the line y=mx. The diagram shows three adjacent squares resting on r1, with the upper-left vertex of each square lying on r2; their side lengths increase from left to right. From the text, the first two side lengths are 20 and 22. If a square has side length s and its left edge is at x, then its upper-left vertex gives s=mx. The next square begins at x+s, so its side length is m(x+s)=mx+ms=s(1+m). Thus consecutive side lengths have constant ratio 1+m. Since 22/20=1.1, the largest side length is 22(1.1)=24.2.

method.method_draft: Use similar triangles and distances along the base. From the image, define d1,d2,d3 as the horizontal distances from the common ray endpoint to the left side of the first, second, and third squares. Because each square’s upper-left corner lies on the same ray r2, the right triangles formed by the endpoint, the left edge of a square, and that square’s top-left corner are all similar. Therefore d_i/s_i is a constant c for each square. The squares are adjacent along r1, so d2-d1=s1 and d3-d2=s2. From the text and image order, s1=20 and s2=22. Since d_i=c s_i, we get c(22-20)=20, so c=10. Then c(s3-22)=22, giving s3-22=2.2 and s3=24.2.
